title: Biotransport / Fluid Mechanics
description: Biotransport / Fluid Mechanics applies conservation laws, fluid mechanics, and mass and heat transfer to living systems and biomedical devices—from physiological pressure and vessel flow through diffusion, membranes, thermoregulation, hemodynamics, and design analysis.

topics.title: Conservation Laws and Biological Control Volumes
topics.description: The course begins with the bookkeeping laws that make biological transport quantitative: what enters, leaves, accumulates, and reacts inside a chosen biological region.

children.title: Control volumes and system boundaries
children.description: This is the habit of drawing the right boundary around a vessel segment, organ compartment, device, or cell layer so a transport problem becomes solvable.

children.title: Choosing boundaries for vessels, lungs, kidneys, and bioreactors
Mass conservation
children.description: Mass balances explain how flow rates, concentrations, and accumulation connect in physiological and engineered systems.

children.title: Source and sink terms for reactions or exchange
Momentum conservation
children.description: Momentum balances turn forces and pressure differences into predictions of flow and shear.

children.title: Wall shear stress as a biological signal
Energy conservation
children.description: Energy balances show when heat, work, and internal energy matter in perfusion, thermal therapies, and device operation.

topics.title: Fluid Statics and Physiological Pressure Fields
topics.description: Static pressure is the simplest fluid-mechanics idea, but it is central to blood pressure, cerebrospinal fluid pressure, edema, ocular pressure, and device calibration.

children.title: Hydrostatic pressure
children.description: Hydrostatics explains how pressure changes with height and density before flow even begins.

children.title: Pressure measurement
children.description: Students learn how pressure values are obtained and interpreted in clinical and experimental contexts.

children.title: Pressure forces on surfaces
children.description: Pressure fields create net forces on valves, vessel walls, and biomedical device components.

children.title: Resultant force and center of pressure
Buoyancy and body forces
children.description: Body-force concepts help explain sedimentation, centrifugation, and density-driven separation.

topics.title: Fluid Properties, Viscosity, and Constitutive Models
topics.description: Biological fluids are often not simple water-like liquids. This section connects measurable properties to the equations used later in the course.

children.title: Density, viscosity, and surface tension
children.description: These properties set the scale of pressure drop, shear stress, capillary effects, and device behavior.

children.title: Newtonian fluids
children.description: Newtonian models are the first approximation for plasma, saline, and many dilute biological fluids.

children.title: Non-Newtonian biological fluids
children.description: Blood, mucus, synovial fluid, and cell suspensions often require richer models.

children.title: Constitutive model selection
children.description: Model choice matters because a simple equation can either clarify the physics or hide the dominant behavior.

topics.title: Governing Equations: Navier-Stokes and Simplifications
topics.description: The governing equations unify the conservation laws with material behavior. Students learn when to use the full equations and when a simpler form is more useful.

children.title: Kinematics of flow
children.description: Kinematics describes motion before asking what caused it, giving students the language of velocity fields and deformation.

children.title: Navier-Stokes Equations
children.description: The Navier-Stokes equations encode mass and momentum transport for viscous fluids.

children.title: Common simplifications
children.description: Most useful biomedical calculations come from carefully justified simplifications.

children.title: Boundary conditions in biological systems
children.description: Biological boundaries can move, slip, deform, or exchange mass, so boundary conditions need physical interpretation.

topics.title: Laminar Internal Flow in Pipes and Blood Vessels
topics.description: Internal flow models provide the first quantitative bridge from pressure gradients to flow rates in vessels, catheters, tubing, and microfluidic channels.

children.title: Poiseuille Flow
children.description: Poiseuille flow gives a clean model for how vessel radius, viscosity, and pressure gradient control flow rate.

children.title: Pressure drop and hydraulic resistance
children.description: Resistance concepts let students treat vascular networks and devices with circuit-like intuition.

children.title: Minor losses in fittings and junctions
Wall shear stress
children.description: Shear stress affects endothelial biology, platelet activation, and device safety.

children.title: Pulsatile and compliant-vessel flow
children.description: Cardiovascular flow is time-varying and vessel walls are elastic, so steady rigid-tube models need careful extension.

topics.title: Dimensional Analysis, Scaling, and Similarity
topics.description: Scaling helps students decide what terms matter, compare systems of different sizes, and design experiments that preserve the important physics.

children.title: Dimensional homogeneity
children.description: Checking dimensions catches errors and reveals useful parameter groupings.

children.title: Key dimensionless numbers
children.description: Dimensionless groups summarize competing transport mechanisms.

children.title: Scaling laws in physiology
children.description: Scaling connects microvascular, organ-level, and whole-body transport behavior.

children.title: Similarity and model design
children.description: Similarity rules help students build bench experiments and computational models that mean something biologically.

topics.title: Diffusion, Convection, and Mass Transfer
topics.description: Mass transfer is the language of oxygen delivery, solute clearance, nutrient supply, metabolite removal, and transport-limited therapy.

children.title: Fickian Diffusion
children.description: Diffusion describes molecular spreading driven by concentration gradients.

children.title: Convective transport
children.description: Convection moves material with the fluid and often dominates in blood flow and perfused devices.

children.title: Convection-diffusion competition
children.description: Students learn to identify whether transport is diffusion-limited, flow-limited, or mixed.

children.title: Mass-transfer coefficients
children.description: Coefficient models turn complex boundary-layer behavior into practical engineering calculations.

topics.title: Transport Across Membranes and Porous Biological Media
topics.description: Many biological barriers behave like membranes or porous media, including capillaries, epithelium, dialysis membranes, tissues, and scaffolds.

children.title: Membrane permeability
children.description: Permeability relates concentration differences to flux across a selective barrier.

children.title: Osmosis and filtration
children.description: Osmotic and hydraulic driving forces explain fluid exchange in capillaries, kidneys, and dialysis.

children.title: Porous-media flow
children.description: Porous-media models describe transport through tissues, gels, scaffolds, and packed-cell regions.

children.title: Coupled solute and fluid transport
children.description: Membranes and tissues often couple pressure-driven flow with diffusion and binding.

topics.title: Heat Transfer and Thermoregulation
topics.description: Heat transfer matters in physiology, implants, cryopreservation, hyperthermia, ablation, and thermal safety for medical devices.

children.title: Conduction in tissue
children.description: Conduction models explain how heat spreads through tissue when perfusion or convection is limited.

children.title: Convection and perfusion
children.description: Blood flow can remove or deliver heat, changing temperature fields dramatically.

children.title: Thermal boundary conditions
children.description: Boundary assumptions determine whether a model represents skin cooling, device heating, or internal therapy.

children.title: Biomedical thermal applications
children.description: Applications show why thermal transport must be controlled rather than treated as a side effect.

topics.title: Microcirculation, Hemodynamics, and Respiratory Transport
topics.description: This section applies core transport principles to the cardiovascular and pulmonary systems where flow, exchange, and geometry are tightly coupled.

children.title: Microvascular flow
children.description: Small-vessel flow introduces cell-scale effects that are invisible in large-pipe models.

children.title: Hemodynamics in larger vessels
children.description: Large-vessel flow connects pressure, pulsatility, wall shear, and vascular disease.

children.title: Respiratory gas exchange
children.description: Gas exchange combines diffusion, convection, and reaction with hemoglobin.

children.title: Clinical interpretation
children.description: Transport models help interpret measurements and pathologies without oversimplifying physiology.

topics.title: Drug Delivery, Bioreactors, and Tissue Transport Cases
topics.description: Case studies turn transport principles into design tools for therapies, devices, engineered tissues, and experimental platforms.

children.title: Drug transport and release
children.description: Drug-delivery problems require coupling release kinetics, diffusion, convection, and biological barriers.

children.title: Bioreactor transport
children.description: Bioreactors must deliver oxygen and nutrients while controlling shear and waste removal.

children.title: Tissue-engineering transport
children.description: Engineered tissues fail if cells are too far from oxygen and nutrient supply.

children.title: Biomedical device design cases
children.description: Device examples help students practice translating models into design constraints.

topics.title: Measurement, Modeling, and Design Analysis
topics.description: The final topic makes the course practical: students learn how to measure transport, validate models, and communicate design tradeoffs.

children.title: Experimental measurement
children.description: Measurement methods teach students how transport quantities are observed and what uncertainty comes with them.

children.title: Particle image velocimetry and tracer methods
Computational modeling
children.description: Computational tools extend analytical models to realistic geometries and coupled physics.

children.title: Parameter estimation
children.description: Biomedical transport models often depend on parameters that must be inferred from data.

children.title: Design communication
children.description: Engineering judgment is demonstrated by explaining assumptions, limits, and consequences clearly.
